es: Distinguir causa, correlación y posibilidad con el verbo adecuado (causes, is linked to, may account for) y corregir causas exageradas.

vocabulary.es: causalidad, relación de causa y efecto
no necesariamente, no tiene por qué

teaching.en: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.
teaching.es: Una correlación muestra que dos mediciones se mueven juntas, pero la causalidad necesita un mecanismo que explique por qué una produce la otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Correlation y causation son incontables; se contrastan con but.
segments: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation
needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.
teaching.audioText: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.

teaching.en: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.
teaching.es: Las ventas de helados y los accidentes al nadar muestran un aumento brusco en julio, pero la correlación es espuria, pues el calor impulsa ambos.
teaching.explanationEs: Spurious: dos datos coinciden sin que uno influya en el otro.
segments: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in
July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.
teaching.audioText: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.

teaching.en: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.
teaching.es: Varios estudios confirman la tendencia de fondo, pero no se deduce necesariamente que hayamos encontrado la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Does not necessarily + verbo base: «no tiene por qué».
segments: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does
not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.
teaching.audioText: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.

teaching.en: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link of that kind is not the same as a cause.
teaching.es: Dormir mal está relacionado con notas más bajas, pero un vínculo así no es lo mismo que una causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Is linked to describe una relación observada, sin decir qué provoca qué.
segments: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link
of that kind is not the same as a cause.
teaching.audioText: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link of that kind is not the same as a cause.

teaching.en: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.
teaching.es: La enfermedad es un factor que contribuye, no la única causa: provoca clases perdidas, que pueden explicar parte de la caída.
teaching.explanationEs: Leads to afirma un efecto; may account for deja una explicación posible.
segments: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads
to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.
teaching.audioText: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.

teaching.en: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together, so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.
teaching.es: Puede ser pura casualidad que dos gráficos se muevan juntos, así que los autores cuidadosos evitan decir que uno causa el otro.
teaching.explanationEs: Coincidence = casualidad; el modal may marca duda.
segments: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together,
so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.
teaching.audioText: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together, so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase resume el resultado del estudio sin exagerar?

choices.text: Sleep is linked to better scores, but other factors may matter too.
Sleep causes better exam scores, as the study clearly shows for every group.
Better exam scores lead to longer sleep, according to the researchers involved.

feedback.es: El estudio no controló dieta, estrés ni ingresos, así que solo permite hablar de una relación y de otros factores posibles.

hint.es: Elige la frase que describe una relación y deja abiertos otros factores.

origin.text: Researchers tracked 2,000 students for a year. Those who slept more than eight hours scored higher in every exam, but the study did not control for diet, stress or family income.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quizá el nuevo carril explique parte de la mejora.»

feedback.es: Account for + sustantivo presenta una explicación posible; el modal may mantiene la cautela y la segunda frase ofrece otra causa.

hint.es: Verbo frasal que significa «explicar» y se construye con for.

origin.text: After the new bus lane opened, journeys became faster. The lane may ___ for part of the improvement, although the repairs ended at the same time.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las dos tendencias podrían ser una simple casualidad.»

answer.text: The two trends could simply be a coincidence
accepted: The two trends could simply be a coincidence
The two trends could be simply a coincidence

feedback.es: Could + simply + be + a coincidence: el modal de duda y el adverbio suavizan la afirmación.

hint.es: El modal could va antes de simply y del verbo be.

prompt.es: ¿Qué error de razonamiento comete el autor del texto?

choices.text: He compares cities of very different sizes without adjusting the figures.
He treats a correlation between two figures as proof of a cause.
He assumes the trend is a pure coincidence without looking at the figures.
He overlooks that school results have risen sharply in every city.

feedback.es: El autor pasa de «más bibliotecas, mejores resultados» a «las bibliotecas mejoran los resultados» sin mecanismo ni otros factores: confunde una correlación con una causa.

origin.text: Cities with more libraries have better school results. Libraries therefore improve results, and councils should open ten more. Nobody has asked whether richer cities simply have both more libraries and better schools.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la economista sobre cafeterías y empresas nuevas.

choices.text: Cafés help start-ups, although the headline overstates the effect.
The link is a coincidence produced by the way cities were chosen.
A third factor, local income, probably explains both.
Start-ups attract cafés, so the direction of cause is reversed.

feedback.es: Para ella, los ingresos locales son el factor que contribuye a ambos hechos; no dice que los cafés ayuden ni que la relación sea casual.

origin.audio: A newspaper reports that cities with more cafés have more start-ups, and concludes that coffee shops help new companies to grow. The expert interviewed is not convinced. She says the link is real, but richer districts attract both cafés and new companies. In her view, local income is a contributing factor that explains both, and the headline ignores it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el nivel de certeza que transmite.

pairs: Sleep is linked to better marks.
Illness may account for the fall.
The link is a spurious correlation.

feedback.es: Cada frase comunica un nivel distinto: causa, relación, posibilidad y correlación espuria.

pairs: Sleep is linked to better marks.
Illness may account for the fall.
The link is a spurious correlation.

prompt.es: Completa: causa comprobada en la primera frase y factor contribuyente en la segunda.

feedback.es: La primera frase afirma una causa probada con leads to; la segunda presenta los ingresos como contributing factor, no como causa única.

sentences: Three large trials show that chronic sleep loss ___ to a drop in attention in class.
Family income is probably a contributing ___ in both trends, so the link is not proven.
origin.text: A health agency reviewed the research on sleep and school results.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la postura de la presentadora ante la afirmación del municipio.

choices.text: The cameras probably did nothing, since other changes explain the drop.
The council is wrong, because accidents fell on similar roads too.
The drop is certainly a coincidence, so the cameras deserve no credit.
The cameras may have helped, but the evidence does not prove it.

feedback.es: Admite que las cámaras podrían explicar parte de la caída, pero pide una comparación: no la descarta ni la da por probada.

origin.audio: When the city installed speed cameras on Harbour Road, serious accidents fell by a third in two years, and the council was quick to claim the credit. I am not so sure. Over the same period the road was repaired, a new bridge opened, and a petrol price rise kept many drivers at home. Each of these could be a contributing factor. The cameras may well account for part of the drop, and I would not rule that out. But to say they caused it, on these figures alone, is to mistake a sharp fall for proof. What we need is a comparison with a similar road that received no cameras.

prompt.es: Corrige este titular exagerado con una relación y una duda razonable.

answer.text: Late-night phone use may be linked to anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could also account for it.
accepted: Late-night phone use may be linked to anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could also account for it.
Using phones at night might be associated with anxiety in teenagers, but other contributing factors may account for it.
There may be a correlation between late-night phones and anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could account for it.

feedback.es: Un titular exagerado se corrige con is linked to, associated with o correlation, un modal de duda y una mención a otros factores.

origin.text: Titular: «Los celulares de noche causan ansiedad en los adolescentes.» Reescríbelo con una relación y un modal de duda, y menciona que otros factores podrían explicarlo.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El fuerte aumento de precios puede explicar ambas tendencias.»

answer.text: The strong rise in prices may account for both trends

feedback.es: May account for presenta el aumento de precios como explicación posible de las dos tendencias.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito aparece la última frase del texto?

choices.text: To warn that the link may work in the opposite direction.
To show that feeling lonely makes adults less able to care for a dog.
To argue that adopting a dog is still the best answer to loneliness.
To suggest that the figures are a coincidence without any meaning.

feedback.es: La frase final propone que la causalidad podría ir al revés: quienes ya se sienten bien adoptan más perros.

origin.text: The figures are striking: in towns where more people own a dog, fewer adults report feeling lonely. Nobody should conclude, however, that adopting a dog is an answer to loneliness. People who already feel well may simply be readier to take one on, and the direction of cause may run the other way.

prompt.es: Completa: «La correlación es espuria: los mayores calzan más y leen mejor.»

feedback.es: Una correlación spurious aparece cuando un tercer factor (la edad) explica ambos datos y no hay conexión real entre ellos.

origin.text: Shoe size and reading ability are strongly linked in primary schools. The correlation is ___, because older children simply have bigger feet and also read better.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La correlación espuria desapareció al incluir el calor.»

answer.text: The spurious correlation disappeared once the heat was included
accepted: The spurious correlation disappeared once the heat was included
Once the heat was included the spurious correlation disappeared

feedback.es: Once introduce la condición que hizo desaparecer la correlación: al incluir el calor, el vínculo dejó de existir.
